page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 machine family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-standard-4 in the lower performance tiers for compute-intensive tasks. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Similarly, Geekbench scores for single-core and multi-core operations are positioned in the bottom 10%, reflecting its design as a cost-efficient rather than high-performance resource. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 24.13 GB/sec and write speeds of 20.93 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, which also rank in the bottom 25%.

Despite these performance constraints, the instance demonstrates average text generation speeds of 104.71 tokens/sec during LLM inference with a small 135M model, though prompt processing remains weak at 258.44 tokens/sec. The primary tradeoff of the e2-standard-4 is its modest processing power in exchange for resource density and qualitative cost efficiency. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, such as basic web serving, small database operations, development environments, and low-intensity background utility tasks that do not require high-frequency compute or local SSD storage.
